My ranking only determines which school I receive *within* that fixed set, specifically my highest-ranked school among the obtainable ones.

Therefore, there is no strategic advantage to misrepresenting my true preferences. Conversely, if I rank a school higher than my true preference, but it's not in my obtainable set, it makes no difference. If it *is* in my obtainable set, and it's my highest ranked *among the obtainable ones*, I get it. If I truly prefer another school more, and that school is also obtainable, I would have gotten it anyway by ranking it higher.

Since my goal is to get the school I prefer most, and my ranking doesn't influence the set of schools I can get, the optimal strategy is to submit my true preferences. This ensures that if my most preferred school is obtainable, I will get it. If it's not, I will get my second most preferred school among the obtainable ones, and so on.

My true preference ordering is explicitly given as: w > x > y > z.
